Thanks for the demo today, Rafael — useful talk. A couple quick follow-ups from our side as we triage Dedicated vs managed hosted for this use case. High level: we want predictable latency for our customer-facing chat (SLA target for p95 generated tokens) and the ability to support concurrent sessions during peak.

Numbers we want to validate:
- p95 latency for short chat (<= 128 tokens output) should be < 400ms end-to-end
- sustained throughput target: 2000 requests/minute during peak 30-minute windows
- concurrency: 150 active chat sessions with streaming responses enabled
- model: prefer Llama-3-70B quantized, but open to alternatives if latency/throughput wins

We also have procurement questions — expected contract length, reserved throughput vs burst, and whether you can guarantee region-specific capacity (us-west). Can you loop in the perf/solutions folks and share any benchmark docs for GPU type comparisons and recommended sizing?

Thanks,
Emily Chen

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Hi all — quick technical readout based on the requirements. High level: Dedicated pools can meet the targets, but sizing depends on the exact model variant (quantization) and whether streaming is required for all requests. Short answers to Rafael's Qs below, then a recommended starting config.

Q1 (latency budget): We recommend Redwood target ~300ms server-side p95 to allow for client network + streaming overhead. That gives ~100ms headroom for websocket and client render in most regions.

Q2 (token distribution): Please confirm distribution — I'm assuming 70% <=128 tokens, 25% between 128-512, 5% >512 for sizing. If you have telemetry we can use that.

Q3 (concurrency): If 150 are actively generating simultaneously, we size for peak concurrency. If many hold idle streams, we can use prefix caching and connection multiplexing to reduce memory footprint but reserved throughput planning still needs to account for active generators.

Initial recommended Dedicated configuration (us-west):
- Model: Llama-3-70B (8-bit quantized recommended to balance quality/latency)
- GPU candidates tested: A100 80GB (best throughput/cost ratio), H100 80GB (best latency at higher cost), and 4xA10G (cheaper, shard-friendly for throughput)
- Reserved throughput guidance: start with reserved QPS = 35 requests/sec (2100 requests/min) — aligns with your 2000 req/min and gives a ~5-10% buffer for bursts
- Instance sizing: for quantized 70B, expect ~1 x H100 (80GB) or 2 x A100 80GB equivalents to comfortably hit p95 <300ms at 128-token outputs for sustained 35 QPS with batching. If you want a cheaper config, 4xA10G with sharding can reach throughput but expect p95 to increase ~20-40ms compared to H100 for small token outputs.
- Streaming: enabling server-side streaming adds ~10-40ms to p95 depending on chunking frequency; we can tune chunk size to trade latency vs throughput.

Attachments: I've added a short GPU comparison PDF (Redwood_Dedicated_GPU_Comparison.pdf) and a proposed sizing workbook (proposed_map_v1.xlsx).

Proposed validation run: 24-hour sustained run at 35 QPS with your token distribution, plus two 30-minute stress windows at 50 QPS. We will collect p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and latency breakdowns (kernel time, queueing, networking). After the run we'll share the report and suggested commit level.

If that plan looks good, Rafael — can you confirm dates for a validation window next week? Emily — I'll need a short set of ~30 representative prompts and a workload trace (or synthetic profile) to replay.

Thanks,
Aditya
Perf Engineer | Redwood Inference
